purpose: Determine whether deterministic history-level nonparallelism appears before the genotype-density closure enters sub-individual mass regimes.
primary_endpoints: terminal density mass for every depression x history x start x arm
far-minus-near inherited-investment effect for every depression x history x start
history labels across the three starts at epsilon 0 and epsilon 0.01

interpretability.pre_quasi_extinction_history: all six terminal masses (3 starts x near/far) are >= 1 expected individual
interpretability.central_question: Does any mixed or positive history occur among pre-quasi-extinction histories?
interpretability.positive_result: at least one mixed or positive history at epsilon 0.01 while all six masses for that history are >=1
interpretability.negative_result: mixed/positive labels occur only in histories where at least one terminal mass is <1, or no mixed/positive labels occur

stopping: all four depression levels must be executed and reported; no outcome-dependent extension or threshold change
claim_boundary: The scan is post-diagnostic but prospectively frozen before intermediate depression outcomes are inspected.
Mass >=1 is only a minimum non-sub-individual condition, not proof of realistic natural persistence.
The deterministic closure is not the stochastic mean of the finite ABM.
A positive scan result would establish model-internal deterministic nonparallelism before sub-individual mass, not natural prevalence or a natural depression threshold.
A negative result demotes the depression-0.75 nonparallelism result from the EL headline.
